office_does: The coroner investigates sudden, violent, suspicious and unexplained deaths in Lewis County and determines their cause and manner.
race_blurb: Coroner Warren McLeod, a Republican in office since 2011, seeks what he says will be his final term against independent Jessica Stickley, a former Lewis County deputy coroner. Stickley campaigns on investigation standards, transparency and prevention. McLeod took 54.4% in the primary.

candidates.summary: Lewis County Coroner since 2011 and former Nevada coroner's investigator and Boston-area EMT; says this would be his last term.
highlights: Coroner since 2011, unopposed after his first election [S2]
Says the office has been accredited since 2012 and its staff are certified death investigators [S1]
Final-term goals: keep accreditation, certify all deputies and turn casual on-call staff into county employees [S2]
Endorsed by the Lewis County Republican Party and coroners of Thurston, Grant and Benton counties [S2]

experience.basis: Sixteen-year incumbent running on the office's accreditation, certifications and continuity.

spending.basis: Plans to keep pressing commissioners for funding to convert casual on-call staff into full- or part-time benefited county positions.

candidates.summary: Medicolegal death investigator and former Lewis County deputy coroner (2009-2019) running as an independent on investigation standards, transparency and death prevention.
highlights: About 15 years in death investigation in Lewis, Cowlitz and Columbia counties [S1][S4]
Cites concerns over controversial investigations, including the Christensen case, and pledges national investigative standards [S4][S2]
Promises more transparency, accountability for mistakes and aftercare for families [S2][S3]
Wants the office to lead prevention of suicides, overdoses and other avoidable deaths [S2][S4]

experience.basis: First-time candidate challenging a 16-year incumbent on change and accountability for the office's mistakes, though she brings about 15 years in the field.
